top_stories.title: Amodei Rejects AI Governing Society; Defends Anthropic's Safety Stance
points: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said humans should not hand society's big decisions to AI, calling the idea he wants humans to surrender free will 'absurd'.
He distinguished between AI doing specific tasks (driving cars, designing cancer drugs, writing software)—which he supports—versus AI writing the rules people live under, which he opposes.

He advocated governing AI through legitimate democratic processes, with some deployments possibly warranting slowdowns or halts to limit job disruption and prevent AI from autonomously building more powerful AI.
Amodei pushed back on a report suggesting Anthropic backs ceding governance to AI, calling rivals' positioning 'vibes-based' and framing Anthropic as the safety leader.

unique_angles.point: Report also noted Anthropic and OpenAI employees privately worry some unreleased internal models may be too powerful to safely release, prompting Democratic senators to call for new AI restrictions.

top_stories.title: SpaceX Wins FCC Approval for Orbital AI Data-Center Satellite Constellation
points: FCC approved SpaceX's plan (reported as 'Starmind') to deploy up to one million solar-powered satellites forming an orbital AI data-center network.
First launches targeted for 2027 with full deployment by 2040, moving energy-intensive computing off-planet.
Potential customers could include AI labs like Anthropic and Google, easing terrestrial power and cooling demands.
Plan faced opposition from Amazon, Viasat, and astronomers over concerns like light pollution, but regulatory approval proceeded.

items.title: OpenAI Warns Heavy ChatGPT Users May Hit Rate Limits Sooner
points: OpenAI said heavy users may encounter limits sooner once Chat and Work usage merge into a single meter.
Rollout expands in December after initial pilots, affecting a small share of power users who consume large query volumes.

items.title: Claude Gains Skills via MCP Servers (Public Beta)
points: Claude users can connect the model to external apps through MCP servers (Model Context Protocol—a standard letting AI connect to external tools without custom integrations) without separate installation.
Feature is now in public beta, enabled by default for Pro, Max, and Ultra users.

items.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang Returns Amid China Espionage Investigation
points: Huang's return added $1 trillion to Nvidia's stock value, with presidential lobbying reportedly playing a role in his reinstatement.

Investigators suspect Megaspeed, a firm connected to Alice Huang (Huang's romantic interest), helped Nvidia hardware reach China; she was in contact with Chinese intelligence though no proof she was directed to extract secrets.
The U.S. blacklisted Megaspeed this week; Congressional hearings begin December 3 on both espionage ties and potential export violations.

items.title: AI Uncovers Decade-Old Software Bugs, Fueling Security Arms Race
points: AI is now highly effective at finding bugs that sat unnoticed in critical software and infrastructure for a decade or more, exposing weaknesses in the web's foundation.
Defenders are using their own AI tools to find and patch vulnerabilities before attackers exploit them, but the arms race is expected to intensify.
More security incidents are expected as AI-exposed vulnerabilities become inevitable; the gap between discovery and fixes will determine real-world damage.

items.title: AI Labs Race to Solve Famous Math Problems
points: Anthropic's Levent Alpöge claimed Claude solved the Riemann Hypothesis, a $1 million Millennium Prize problem and math's most famous open conjecture.

OpenAI released 700+ AI-written math papers in October plus nine more in November, including a claimed proof on fast matrix multiplication; Google posted six papers from its Gemini-powered research agent.
Mathematicians and AI labs are clashing over credit and verification since proofs are posted to GitHub but not yet peer-reviewed.

items.title: AI-First Startups Show Rapid Global Growth
points: Median six-month revenue for 2025 startups on Stripe Atlas rose 39% versus 2024, with 20% taking payments within 30 days.
42% of new C corporations are building AI products, particularly agents (autonomous AI systems that take actions on their own, unlike passive chatbots).
Top 10% of startups reached 15 countries within six months, suggesting AI products have inherent global reach.

items.title: Developer Builds Auto-Muting TV Ad System Using Claude Vision
points: A developer built an auto-muting TV system for ads using Claude vision (AI's ability to analyze images), processing one screenshot per second of a three-hour game for 5 cents total at 95% first-attempt accuracy.
Scope expanded to include social media feeds and AI-powered radio commentary replacing TV announcers, all built in under 30 minutes.
Key lesson: ask the AI system 'What am I assuming is too hard or too expensive?' since cost/complexity assumptions often don't survive contact with modern AI capabilities.

items.title: Epochal's Time Portal Simulates History for AI Forecasting
points: Founded by former xAI engineers, the tool locks AI agents inside simulated internet environments from any date in the past 30+ years.
Agents use historical data snapshots to make predictions about markets, business results, and world events with reportedly robust accuracy.
Garnered 3.3M views, validating a novel approach to AI-based prediction.

items.title: Nothing's Ear (note) Earbuds Add Built-In AI Recording
points: Records phone calls through the earbuds and captures in-person conversations via microphones in the charging case, even while buds are inside.
Companion app automatically transcribes recordings and generates quick summaries.
Positions as a convenient alternative to standalone AI recorders by integrating into everyday wearables.

items.title: Advertising Backlash Pushes Brands Toward 'Effort Signaling'
points: Coca-Cola's AI-generated holiday ad (70,000 AI clips) and Kalshi's NBA Finals commercial both drew negative reception, signaling consumer backlash against AI-made ads.
Luxury brands are pivoting to 'effort signaling'—showcasing handcrafted quality like stop-motion (Geico), claymation (Levi's), and real actors (Coca-Cola's new campaigns).
Exception: Geico used AI to have its Gecko join a live, unscripted podcast with WNBA player Azzi Fudd, enhancing human talent rather than replacing it, earning positive reception.

items.title: Anthropic Testing Claude Opus 5.6
points: Anthropic is testing Claude Opus 5.6 with select users.
Early reports indicate a significant performance jump over Opus 5.5.

items.title: OpenAI Launches Private Inference for Enterprise
points: OpenAI is rolling out Private Inference to a limited customer group as part of its Private Intelligence offering.
It combines Zero Data Retention (data not stored) with Private Safety Processing (automated safety checks without human review).
Sam Altman claims the system enables safety compliance while keeping underlying content completely inaccessible to OpenAI personnel.

items.title: GPT-6.2 Astra Achieves Superhuman Math Optimization
points: A single agent surpassed all human-designed software on optimization problems spanning quadratic programming, mixed-integer non-linear programming, and semidefinite programming.
The model was allowed internet search access; test cases were open-ended, variable-scale, and drawn from diverse real-world applications.
Performance suggests the model can autonomously solve previously intractable mathematical problems.

items.title: 'Speculative Encoding' Cuts AI Agent Context Costs
points: Agents increasingly pass full context between models as text, and prefill costs (the initial processing pass) grow quadratically with context length.
Speculative encoding directly translates hidden states (internal model representations) between models instead of re-processing text, speeding up response startup while maintaining accuracy.
This eliminates redundant computation since the sending model already computed what the receiving model would otherwise recompute.

items.title: TypeSafe's Jev Model Likely Based on Qwen3.5-35B
points: Latency analysis and architectural patterns suggest TypeSafe's Jev model is built on Qwen3.5-35B.
